diagnostics.message:
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.aws_config_configuration_aggregator.organization` is created with `organization_aggregation_source.role_arn` from `aws_iam_role.config_organization`, so it only waits for the role itself. The aggregator immediately assumes that role to read AWS Organizations, which requires AWSConfigRoleForOrganizations to be attached first (the provider's own organization-aggregator example uses `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.organization]`). `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.config_organization` is a sibling with no ordering relative to the aggregator, so creation can fail with an insufficient-permissions error.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_config_configuration_aggregator.organization` is created with `organization_aggregation_source { role_arn = aws_iam_role.config_organization[0].arn }`, which only guarantees the role exists. The organization aggregator requires that role to already carry the AWSConfigRoleForOrganizations managed policy; the AWS provider's own documented example puts `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.organization]` on the aggregator for exactly this reason. If the aggregator is created before `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.config_organization` completes, aggregator creation fails with an insufficient-permissions error.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`aws_config_configuration_aggregator.organization` only depends on `aws_iam_role.config_organization` (through `role_arn`), but not on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.config_organization`. Creating an organization-source aggregator immediately exercises the role (AWS Config calls EnableAwsServiceAccess against AWS Organizations), so the `AWSConfigRoleForOrganizations` policy must already be attached. Both the AWS and Terraform registry examples for organization aggregation include an explicit `depends_on` on the role-policy attachment for exactly this reason. Without it, the aggregator can be created before the role has any permissions and creation fails with an insufficient-permissions error. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.config_organization]` to `aws_config_configuration_aggregator.organization`.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:module.config_baseline_ap-northeast-1` (and every other `config_baseline_*` region module) only receives `s3_bucket_name = local.audit_log_bucket_id`, which depends on the bucket itself, not on its policy. Enabling the recorder validates that AWS Config can access the audit bucket (`s3:GetBucketAcl`/`s3:PutObject` are granted by `:resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log`), so `aws_config_delivery_channel.bucket` / `aws_config_configuration_recorder_status.recorder` can race ahead of the bucket policy and fail with InsufficientDeliveryPolicyException. This is the same external ordering the CloudTrail module needs (it uses the `cloudtrail_depends_on` variable hack for exactly this bucket policy); the config modules have no equivalent.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`module.config_baseline_ap-northeast-1` is given `s3_bucket_name = local.audit_log_bucket_id` (from `module.audit_log_bucket.this_bucket`) but does not depend on `:resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log`, which grants `config.amazonaws.com` s3:GetBucketAcl/s3:ListBucket/s3:PutObject on that bucket. Starting the configuration recorder before the delivery policy exists fails with InsufficientDeliveryPolicyException. CloudTrail is protected from this by `cloudtrail_depends_on`; AWS Config has no equivalent ordering.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.cloudtrail_baseline:resource.aws_cloudtrail.global` passes `sns_topic_name` from `aws_sns_topic.cloudtrail-sns-topic`, but nothing orders it after `module.cloudtrail_baseline:resource.aws_sns_topic_policy.local-account-cloudtrail`, which is what grants `cloudtrail.amazonaws.com` permission to publish to that topic. Creating the trail before the topic policy exists fails with an invalid / insufficient SNS-topic-policy error. The module's `depends_on` via `var.cloudtrail_depends_on` only covers the S3 bucket policy, not the topic policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_cloudtrail.global` sets `sns_topic_name = aws_sns_topic.cloudtrail-sns-topic[0].arn`, so it waits for the topic but not for `aws_sns_topic_policy.local-account-cloudtrail`, which grants `cloudtrail.amazonaws.com` permission to publish. CloudTrail validates that permission when the trail is created, so the trail can fail with an SNS authorization error unless the topic policy is applied first (the same class of ordering problem the module already handles for the S3 bucket policy via `cloudtrail_depends_on`).
